R._note: Demacian Justice. PATCH 16.15 UPDATE (2026-08-11): BaseDamage was nerfed 150/250/350 -> 125/200/275 (weekly cdragon drift audit, CLAUDE_CODE_TODO 70/72); ExecuteDamage is UNCHANGED. Both terms are now LIVE-MEASURED rather than wiki-quoted -- two practice-tool casts at R rank 1 on a VANILLA rune page (no Axiom) gave 125 on a full-HP 1000/1000 target and 255 on a 480/1000 target, which back-solve to BaseDamage[1]=125 and ExecuteDamage[1]=(255-125)/520=0.2500 with delta 0.0 on both rows, independently reproducing the refreshed BIN arrays. See docs/reports/golden/GOLDEN_03_GAREN.md 6 and GoldenGarenTests.cs. Prior wiki basis, kept for provenance (2026-07-10 fetch of https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Template:Data_Garen/Demacian_Justice): 'True Damage: 150 / 250 / 350 (+ 25 / 30 / 35% of target's missing health)' at ranks 1/2/3, which matched the then-current BIN exactly. Current BIN (communitydragon/garen.bin.json): DataValue 'BaseDamage' = [50, 125, 200, 275, 350, 425, 500] and 'ExecuteDamage' = [0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5] (index==rank per FormulaInterpreter.LookupDataValue's clamp convention), so BaseDamage[1..3]=125/200/275 and ExecuteDamage[1..3]=0.25/0.3/0.35. CURATED AS TWO INDEPENDENT HITS (summed by DamageEngine), not the BIN's own single combined GameCalculation ('{6d548702}' = SumOfSubParts[NamedDataValue(BaseDamage), ProductOfSubParts[StatByNamedDataValue(mStat=15, ExecuteDamage), ProductOfSubParts[NamedDataValue(ExecuteDamage), Number(100)]]]): that combined calc references BIN mStat id 15 (presumably 'target's missing health'), which is NOT one of the ids this codebase's ATTACKER-side stat resolvers (SkillDamage.BuildStatResolver) map (0/1/2/6/movespeed/12 only -- no live 'target missing health' concept exists in that resolver's model), so evaluating it directly would silently fail/return null. Hit 1 below (flatDataValue: BaseDamage) resolves the flat term live via the new SkillDamage.ComputeFlatDataValue (added this session specifically for this case). Hit 2 (hpPercentDataValue: ExecuteDamage, hpBasis: Missing) resolves the missing-health scaling term live via the EXISTING TryBuildHitShape/ComboExecuteType.MissingHp path -- the exact mechanism the user asked to have 'perfectly back-calculated.' HONESTY CAVEAT (see M05_DAMAGE_ENGINE.md v2.6 changelog and Combo/TargetHealthTracker.cs): 'perfectly' is not actually achievable -- the Live Client API never exposes a target's real current/missing HP. This hit's missing-HP term is only as accurate as whatever CurrentHP ComboRunner.BuildDefenderFor resolves for the target: full HP (0% missing, the pre-existing default) unless a TargetHealthTracker is wired in, in which case it is an honest LOWER-BOUND estimate (100% HP anchored at the target's last known respawn, minus our own calculated combo damage dealt since) that can only ever UNDERSTATE real missing health, never overstate it -- narrowed, never closed.

_noteR2: ORDERING FIX (Claude Code, GOLDEN_03_GAREN.md §5 round 2, 2026-07-14): the missing-HP hit now resolves BEFORE the flat hit (was: flat then missing). Both hits fire within the SAME R cast, which the wiki/BIN model as ONE simultaneous instance (150 + 25%missing, both read off the SAME pre-cast HP) — but DamageEngine.Simulate processes a slot's hits as SEQUENTIAL nodes sharing one running HP track, so the OLD order (flat first) had the flat hit's own damage silently inflate what the missing-HP hit then read (e.g. on a FULL-HP target, 0 real missing HP still produced a nonzero missing-hit contribution, because the flat hit landed a moment 'earlier' in the simulated sequence and counted as freshly-missing health). Swapping the order fixes this self-inflicted double-count (missing-HP hit now reads the true pre-R state) while PRESERVING the intended cross-node dynamic re-evaluation (a prior Q/E in the same combo still correctly reduces the HP the missing-HP hit reads — only the relative order of R's OWN two hits changed). Confirmed against the golden sheet: full-HP target (0 missing) + Axiom now gives exactly 168 (was 210 pre-fix); the Q→E→R sequencing-identity and fit-2 (~460 missing → ~297 amped) scenarios in GoldenGarenTests.cs both match post-fix. See also ComboEngine.ApplyAxiomArcanistUltimateMultiplier's own fix (now also scales ExecutePercent, not just Damage/AD/AP ratios) — without it, Axiom silently never amplified this hit at all.
